name: Loom
description: Self-hosted shared memory for coding agents, with namespace-scoped access and revision history.
tagline: Shared memory with provenance and code links
approachDetail: Named memory keys and revisions with semantic, lexical and hybrid retrieval.
searchDetail: Semantic, lexical, reciprocal-rank fusion and BM25 hybrid modes; the server default is semantic.
storageDetail: ClickHouse is required. The default memory authority is ClickHouse; a deployment can instead use PostgreSQL for live memory while ClickHouse retains search projections.
toolSupportDetail: MCP tools work separately from transcript capture; capture and session primers depend on the client integration.
scopesDetail: Organization and namespace scope access; agent, user and session identify authorship and can narrow reads.
duplicateDetail: Same-key idempotency and peer duplicate/conflict checks; semantic behavior depends on configured providers.
retentionDetail: No default lifetime for memory content; writers can set expiry or retire facts, while explicit erasure removes retained content.
multiUserDetail: Authenticated deployments use namespace grants and separate read/write roles. The stock local stack is single-user.
crossMachineDetail: Clients can share one reachable authenticated server; this is not offline file synchronization.
webUiDetail: The server serves a dashboard for memory, search and administration.
tokenBudgetingDetail: Retrieval can limit result count with top_k; this does not guarantee a fixed total token count.
contextInjectionDetail: Coding-agent plugins load a session primer through hooks; other MCP clients call tools explicitly.
networkDetail: Server and database services are required. Released images include a local embedder; external model requests depend on provider configuration.
auditTrailDetail: Memory history exposes revisions, writer and source provenance. Explicit erasure or redaction can remove content.
pros: Namespace-scoped shared memory with separate read/write roles
cons: Requires a running server and ClickHouse
Meaningful extraction and synthesized answers require a configured real LLM
Code-linked memory needs a repository index; changed code calls for rechecking the lesson, not automatic rejection
